question: Can open foundation models automate the expert choices of feature library and optimizer that govern SINDy-based discovery of interpretable dynamical laws from text, tables, and plots?

key_findings.claim: Al-Khwarizmi is an orchestration layer around SINDy rather than a new equation estimator.
key_findings.evidence: An LLM and VLM summarize descriptions, raw trajectories, and plots; an LLM emits PySINDy feature-library and optimizer code; SINDy fits coefficients; RAG, prior attempts, and optional human feedback modify later prompts.

key_findings.claim: The reported aggregate benchmark advantage is invalid as an estimate of held-out generalization because test data are repeatedly used for candidate selection and stopping.
key_findings.evidence: Each one-step condition generates 30 samples and selects the candidate with highest test R2. Reflection again selects by test R2 and terminates once test R2 exceeds 0.99. Table 2 then reports the fraction exceeding thresholds on that same test set.

key_findings.claim: Under the paper's contaminated selection protocol, the full system reports the strongest threshold counts on DYSTS and ODEBench.
key_findings.evidence: The overall condition reports test R2 above 0.99 for 83.0% of DYSTS and 85.7% of ODEBench, versus PySR's 64.4% and 63.5%. Because the overall condition pools RAG, reflection, human feedback, optimizer selection, and special hard-case reruns, it is not a controlled single method budget.

key_findings.claim: RAG and human feedback are not consistently beneficial.
key_findings.evidence: RAG generally improves training fits but test R2 is described as weak and some no-RAG runs outperform RAG. Human feedback provides some benefits but is reported not to yield significant improvements overall.

key_findings.claim: The SINDy representation remains a hard ceiling even when an LLM chooses it.
key_findings.evidence: The method fails to generalize on logistic-like and x log x dynamics because the true functions are not linear combinations of the chosen primitives; symbolic regression sometimes performs better on these one-dimensional systems.

method.core_idea: Use pretrained language and vision models as an automated scientific-modeling assistant that configures a sparse, interpretable estimator.
method.mechanism: Summarize each system's text, CSV trajectory, and plot; retrieve similar examples; prompt an LLM to generate executable feature-library/optimizer code; fit and score SINDy; feed selected attempts and optional human comments into reflection rounds.
assumptions: Foundation-model pretraining contains relevant scientific and software knowledge
Plots and summaries preserve the dynamics needed for library choice
The true law is sparse in some SINDy candidate library
Generated code executes safely and correctly
Test-set feedback is acceptable for the reported objective

techniques.role: Compresses raw trajectories and plots into prompt-compatible descriptions.
Retrieves prior systems and code configurations by text-embedding similarity.
Produces feature-library and optimizer code for a conventional sparse regression backend.
Feeds earlier candidate configurations and scores back to the model for iterative search.

evaluations.metric: percentage with train/test R2 above 0.9 or 0.99
evaluations.result: full pooled condition reports 83.0% and 85.7% test R2>0.99
evaluations.baseline: default PySINDy, PySR, ODEFormer, and a 16-system LLM4ED subset

evaluations.metric: R2 threshold counts and percent improvement
evaluations.result: modal summaries and more examples sometimes help, but test performance is inconsistent
evaluations.baseline: no description, text-only, data-only, and image-only prompts

limitations: Critical evaluation leakage: test R2 controls candidate choice, reflection, and termination.
Author-stated: long prompts force lossy data/plot summaries.
Author-stated: noisy measurements and derivative estimation are not evaluated.
The full condition pools heterogeneous search budgets and hand attention on hard cases.
Generated scientific code creates execution, reproducibility, and security risks not analyzed in the paper.
failure_modes: Repeated test optimization selects spurious equations that interpolate the benchmark split.
A missing primitive makes the correct law unreachable regardless of LLM quality.
RAG retrieves superficially similar but dynamically different systems.
Vision/text summaries omit phase, scale, or derivative information.
Executable code may silently use wrong shapes, units, or evaluation data.
reusable_insights: Keep the symbolic estimator modular and let an agent propose its configuration.
Separate model-search validation data from a never-touched final test set.
An agent cannot overcome a misspecified hypothesis library without a route to expand representation.
open_questions: Does the advantage survive a nested train/validation/test protocol with equal search budgets?
Can dimensional analysis and unit constraints reject plausible but unphysical candidates?
How robust is multimodal library selection to noise, irregular sampling, and partial observability?

competitive_landscape.title: Discovering governing equations from data: Sparse identification of nonlinear dynamical systems
competitive_landscape.difference: SINDy performs sparse regression over an expert-chosen library; Al-Khwarizmi keeps this estimator and automates library/optimizer choices with foundation models.

competitive_landscape.title: LLM4ED: Large Language Models for Automatic Equation Discovery
competitive_landscape.difference: LLM4ED directly proposes and evolves equation strings using score feedback; Al-Khwarizmi instead prompts for SINDy libraries/optimizers and adds multimodal summaries and retrieval.

competitive_landscape.title: ODEFormer: Symbolic Regression of Dynamical Systems with Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: ODEFormer is pretrained end to end to map a trajectory to symbolic ODEs and evaluates noise/irregular sampling; Al-Khwarizmi uses general foundation models to configure SINDy at inference time.

competitive_landscape.title: Automated Statistical Model Discovery with Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: BoxLM proposes executable probabilistic/statistical programs under natural-language constraints and evaluates extrapolation; Al-Khwarizmi specializes the search space to sparse dynamical-system libraries and optimizers.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper introduces a multimodal, retrieval- and reflection-augmented foundation-model agent that automates SINDy and outperforms equation-discovery baselines across 198 systems.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The system integrates open LLM/VLM components, PySINDy code generation, RAG, feedback, and broad benchmark tables.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The orchestration is a novel integration, but the headline performance cannot support a generalization claim because the procedure searches directly on the reported test split. A clean nested evaluation is required before ranking it against ODEFormer, PySR, or LLM4ED.

reviewer_notes: Read all 31 extracted pages, emphasizing the exact selection loop, table protocol, prompts, and limitations. The test-leakage conclusion follows directly from Sections 6.2 and 6.4, not from missing implementation detail. Primary records checked 2026-08-23.
